methodological_rigor.justification: The study uses a large (n=3383) multicenter prospective cohort with pre-specified subgroup analyses and an appropriate time-dependent multivariable Cox model that explicitly addresses immortal-time bias — a critical issue in precision-oncology matched-therapy comparisons. Adjustment covariates (age, ECOG, cancer type, prior lines, prior receipt of matched therapy) are relevant, and sensitivity analyses accounting for pre-results deaths and updated TOPOGRAPH tiering strengthen robustness. Algorithmic tier assignment helps mitigate subjective bias. Weaknesses include lack of a reported a priori power calculation, residual confounding by indication inherent to the design (patients receiving matched therapy are not randomized), small subgroup counts in tiers 1–2 (n=64) and tier 4 driving wide CIs, and absence of multiplicity correction across multiple subgroup comparisons. The 2.4-month median time-to-therapy and the tier-3B delay (167 days) hint at residual time-dependent selection beyond what the time-dependent covariate adjusts.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: This is an individual prospective observational cohort study (Oxford LoE 2b) from a national precision-oncology screening program, with OS — a patient-centered endpoint — as the primary outcome. Clinical relevance is high: the findings directly address a pressing dilemma in precision oncology (whether all biomarker-matched therapies justify use) and support international guidance (e.g., ESMO) against off-label repurposing based on noncognate-histotype evidence (tier 3B). While not practice-changing in isolation, the data are directly applicable to molecular tumor board decision-making for refractory and rare cancers (71.7% of the cohort), a population underserved by RCTs.

reporting_quality.justification: STROBE applies as this is an observational cohort study and the authors explicitly state adherence. The manuscript provides a cohort flow diagram (Figure 1), explicit inclusion/exclusion criteria, prespecified subgroup analyses, trial registration (ACTRN12616000908437), ethics approval, defined endpoints, and detailed statistical methods. Minor gaps include no reported handling of missing covariate data and no formal reporting of lost-to-follow-up by cohort. Data/code availability is not described in the blinded text — no repository, DOI, or code link appears, and the TOPOGRAPH knowledge base version is cited but not linked, so reproducibility posture is limited (score 2).

novelty_literature.justification: The study is a meaningful extension of prior precision-oncology cohort/basket efforts (MOSCATO, WINTHER, MyPathway, TAPUR, I-PREDICT, SHIVA, ProfiLER, Know Your Tumor, ROME) rather than a first-in-class contribution. The specific empirical contribution — demonstrating that only tier 1–3A (prospective-trial-supported) matches confer OS benefit while tier 3B drug repurposing from noncognate histotypes does not — is a credible, actionable refinement that leverages the authors' previously published TOPOGRAPH framework (ref 27). The literature positioning is reasonably complete, though the manuscript could more directly contrast tier-based findings with ESCAT (ref 34) rather than merely acknowledging the comparison as future work.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is well organized with a structured abstract, logical Introduction–Methods–Results–Discussion flow, and informative figure captions. Numeric reporting is thorough with CIs and P values throughout. Some rough edges exist: the subsection heading 'Survival Association Between Harborage of Actionable Biomarkers' is awkward; a numeric value for cohort A appears redacted in the Participant Characteristics paragraph; and some figure-caption aHRs (e.g., Figure 3A 0.76 95% CI 0.70–0.90) differ slightly from text (0.78 95% CI 0.66–0.91), which is a small but concerning inconsistency. Overall clarity is high and the abstract accurately mirrors the key results.

key_strengths: Large (n=3383) national prospective precision-oncology cohort enriched for rare/refractory cancers (71.7%), a historically underserved population
Time-dependent Cox model with adjustment for immortal-time bias and multiple sensitivity analyses (pre-results deaths, updated tiering, same-therapy analysis)
Clinically actionable finding separating tier 1–3A benefit (aHR 0.60) from absence of benefit for tier 3B repurposing (aHR 1.40) — directly informs molecular tumor board practice
Explicit STROBE adherence, pre-specified subgroups, trial registration, and algorithmic tier assignment to limit subjective bias
key_concerns: Residual confounding by indication is inherent and inadequately addressed beyond covariate adjustment; small subgroup Ns (e.g., tier 1–2 n=64) yield wide CIs
No power calculation reported and no multiplicity correction across the multiple tier/subgroup comparisons
Data and code availability not described; TOPOGRAPH knowledge base version cited but not linked, limiting reproducibility
Minor numeric inconsistencies between figure captions and text (Figure 3 aHRs/CIs), and one redacted value in Participant Characteristics
Tier 3B matched patients had a markedly longer delay to therapy (median 167 vs 75 days), suggesting selection effects the model may not fully capture
chief_reviewer.rationale: A methodologically solid, clinically relevant observational cohort with an actionable tiered-matching finding; appropriate for a strong specialty oncology journal (Tier 2) pending clarifications on reproducibility, multiplicity, and figure/text numeric alignment.
